_readme: THE ONE PLACE the comparison table's facts live. tools/compare_table.py renders
it into the <tbody> of the table in src/index.html and into the dated footnote
(cmp.note) in assets/js/i18n.js; check_site.py fails if either is stale, and
warns when checked_on is more than 90 days old.
COMPETITOR cells: "yes" = the maker states the feature on its own site;
"premium" / "pro" = stated as part of that paid plan; "gfit" = Google Fit
rather than Health Connect; a price string; null = NOT stated on the
maker's site on the check date (rendered as —, never as ✗ — absence is
not something we can confirm). A guess never goes in this file.
OUR cell ("fotocal") is held to the same standard we hold them to, and is
read off the APP'S GATING CODE — never off this site's marketing copy, which
is the thing being audited. Values: "yes" = in the free plan, uncapped;
"premium" = needs a subscription, same word we print for MyFitnessPal;
"free2day" / "free1day" = free with that daily cap; "free2" = two free and
the rest behind Premium; "partfree" = free to open with parts behind Premium.
fotocal_why records the file and condition each value was read from. If the
app's gating changes, that column changes here first and the pages follow.

checked_at.Cal AI: https://www.calai.app/ · https://www.calai.app/faq (maker's site; no price published there)

note.en: Competitor columns show what each maker states on its own website, checked on {date}: ✓ or a plan name means the maker states it, — means it is not stated there. Prices are the makers' published yearly prices in US dollars and can change. Fotocal is Android-only for now. The Fotocal column is our own free and Premium line, read off the app rather than written by us: ✓ means the free plan with no cap, Premium means it needs a subscription, and anything else names the limit the free plan has.
note.es: Las columnas de la competencia recogen lo que cada fabricante declara en su propia web, comprobado el {date}: ✓ o el nombre de un plan significa que el fabricante lo declara; — significa que no consta. Los precios son los anuales publicados por cada fabricante, en dólares, y pueden cambiar. Por ahora Fotocal es solo para Android. La columna de Fotocal es nuestra propia línea entre gratis y Premium, leída de la app y no escrita por nosotros: ✓ significa plan gratuito sin tope, Premium significa que necesita suscripción, y cualquier otra cosa nombra el límite que tiene el plan gratuito.

rows.why: Cal AI: photo scan is the product. MFP: Meal Scan is a Premium feature (English only). Yazio: AI food tracking is part of Pro.
Cal AI lists barcode scanning. MFP: barcode scanner Premium-only since Oct 2022. Yazio: barcode is in the free tier (Pro adds AI scanner, analyses, ratings, activity, recipes).
Restaurant menu scanning: none of the three states it.
Cal AI offers typed 'describe', not voice, on its site. MFP: Voice Log is Premium, English only. Yazio: only Siri Shortcuts on iOS, nothing for Android.
AI chat coach: none of the three states it.
Health score with swaps: not stated. Yazio's 'smart food ratings' (Pro) is a different thing and is not counted.
MFP: Nutrient Dashboard is Premium. Yazio: vitamins & minerals are Pro. Cal AI: not stated.
Mood & habit journal: none of the three states it.
MFP: weekly progress views are for Premium members. Yazio: weekly/monthly evaluation is Pro-only (free has daily). Cal AI: not stated.
Cal AI: connects to Google Fit on Android (Health Connect not named). MFP: Health Connect documented. Yazio: Health Connect documented, automatic activity tracking is a Pro feature.
MFP and Yazio both list Spanish among app languages. Cal AI: languages not stated.

MFP: Premium $79.99/yr (Premium+ $99.99/yr). Cal AI: no price on its site. Yazio: prices vary by country and no yearly figure is published on the pages reachable; the ≈$44 and $47.90 the table used to show are gone.
